In 1263 CE, the Pandya king Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I defeated Ganapatideva during his southern campaign. s: Who among the following used the title 'Rayagaja Kesari'
x:
Prataparudra II, the last great ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty, bore the title "Rayagajakesari." The title literally means "a lion among kings and elephants," symbolizing bravery, military strength and royal supremacy. Prataparudra successfully defended the Kakatiya kingdom against several invasions before finally being defeated by Ulugh Khan in 1323 CE. His reign represents the final phase of Kakatiya political power.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who built the lake Kesari Samudra?
x:
Kesari Samudram is a historic irrigation tank constructed during the Kakatiya period by Rudradeva, one of the earliest powerful rulers of the Kakatiya dynasty. The Kakatiyas were renowned for their emphasis on irrigation development. They built hundreds of tanks and reservoirs to conserve rainwater and support agriculture in the dry regions of Telangana. Kesari Samudram is one such engineering achievement that contributed significantly to agricultural prosperity. The Kakatiya rulers considered irrigation as the backbone of their economy, and their tank- building tradition continues to benefit the region even today.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Which Kakatiya ruler shifted the capital from Hanamkonda to Orugallu?
x:
Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) was the first powerful independent ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty. During his reign, he shifted the capital from Hanamkonda to Orugallu (present-day Warangal). The new capital was strategically stronger and better suited for administration and defence. Rudradeva strengthened the fortifications of Orugallu and laid the foundation for its development into one of the greatest capitals in medieval South India. Later rulers, particularly Ganapatideva and Rani Rudramadevi, further expanded and beautified Warangal, making it the political and cultural centre of the Kakatiya kingdom.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Which ruler issued the famous Motupalli Charter?
x:
Ganapatideva, one of the greatest rulers of the Kakatiya dynasty, issued the famous Motupalli Charter to encourage overseas trade. The charter granted commercial privileges, protection and tax concessions to foreign merchants visiting the port of Motupalli. It assured traders of safety and promoted maritime commerce with countries such as China, Sri Lanka, Arabia and Southeast Asia. The Motupalli Charter reflects the Kakatiyas' farsighted economic policy and highlights the importance of maritime trade in medieval Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: For the first time, in which inscription were the Kakatiyas mentioned?
x:
The Magallu Inscription provides the earliest epigraphic reference to the Kakatiya dynasty. The inscription mentions Beta I, an early Kakatiya chief, and is regarded as the earliest reliable source for tracing the origin and genealogy of the Kakatiyas. It marks the beginning of the recorded history of one of the greatest dynasties of medieval Andhra and Telangana. Subsequent inscriptions such as the Bayyaram Inscription provide more detailed genealogical information, but the Magallu Inscription remains the earliest reference.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Importance – First epigraphic mention of the Kakatiyas

s: Who built the lake of Arikesari Samudram?
x:
Prolaraja II, one of the prominent early Kakatiya rulers, is credited with constructing the Arikesari Samudram tank. The Kakatiyas gave great importance to irrigation by constructing numerous tanks, lakes and reservoirs. These irrigation works significantly improved agriculture and earned the Kakatiyas a lasting reputation as builders of tanks.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who among the following was awarded the title 'Founder of Kakati Rajya'?
x:
Recherla Rudra was one of the most distinguished military commanders of the Kakatiya kingdom. After the death of Rudradeva, he played a crucial role in protecting the kingdom from external invasions and internal rebellions. During the captivity of Ganapatideva by the Yadavas, Recherla Rudra safeguarded the kingdom and later helped restore Kakatiya authority. For his immense contribution in strengthening and consolidating the Kakatiya kingdom, he was honored with the title "Kakati Rajya Sthapanacharya" (Founder/Restorer of the Kakatiya Kingdom). His services were instrumental in transforming the Kakatiyas into a powerful medieval empire.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
x:
The title "Mahamandaleswara" literally means "Great Lord of Provinces". During the early phase of their political career, the Kakatiya rulers, while serving as feudatories under the Western Chalukyas, frequently used this title. It denoted powerful provincial governors or feudatory chiefs controlling large territories. Even after attaining independence, the title continued to appear in several Kakatiya inscriptions as a mark of prestige and authority.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
n: Mahamandaleswara → Prominent title of early Kakatiyas
